title: Reviewed exceptions
description: Schema for .ci/exceptions.yml, per docs/gitlab-ci-agent-standard.md section 3. The file is a record, not an enforcement mechanism: nothing reads it at pipeline time, and deleting an entry does not undo the deviation it describes. What the schema enforces is that an accepted deviation carries the four things a reviewer needs to act on it later — what it covers, which rule it excepts, who owns it, and when it lapses.

date.description: yyyy/mm/dd. An exception with no expiry is a decision and belongs in the standard or an ADR instead, so 'unresolved' is not accepted here.

sentence.description: Prose a reviewer who was not there can act on. Not a label.

id.description: EXC-nnnn. The same pattern a consumer's .ci/project.yml uses in its exceptions list, so an id written there resolves here.

scope.description: What the exception covers: a path, a template, a consumer project, or the whole repository.

rule.description: The rule being excepted, quoted from the standard and prefixed with its section number.

owner.description: The person accountable for closing it. An exception nobody owns does not close.

compensating_controls.description: What limits the risk while the exception stands, or the single item 'none' to say plainly that nothing does.
